rows.etymology: 1126. Bng. bardlɔ ‘rainy (German: verregnet)’ (with -lɔ suffix) and Dari. bhidla ‘wet’ (with spontaneous aspiration) < OIA *vyārdra-; note that the lemma ārdrá- ‘wet’ (1340) has preserved -rd- mostly in the northwest (but there is also Garh. ād ‘wet’ and Brj. ādhi ‘steam’). To be added to this group is Sir.ḍoḍ. andrerṇo ‘gīlā karnā – to make wet’ (Kaul [2006 ii: 327]). There is a parallel to the Bng. word in Kal. j̣ac̣aḷóa ‘rainy, snowy, inclement’: a change of vy- > ǰ is known from different Paš. dialects: ǰaṅg ‘hobbling’ < vyàṅga- - ‘crippled’ (12158), ǰāvä ‘main roof-beam’ < OIA *vyāpā- ‘widely extending (beam)’ (12204) (this word has a parallel in Kal. ǰav gren ‘top layer of beams in wall of a building which ties the structure together’; gren means ‘joint of two beams in a wall’ and derives < OIA granthí- ‘joint’ [4354], see there also Kho. gren ‘log in a wall’); the first Kal. retroflex is due to CCH and the second displays a case of devoicing, and both words (bardlɔ and j̣ac̣aḷóa) have a suffix with a lateral. Note: Instead of -c̣- a -ǰ̣- should have been expected, but c.f. e.g. Kal. čhu ‘daugh- ter’ < OIA duhitŕ̥- ‘daughter’ (6481).
